newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek markets jubilant on central bank rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Greek markets jubilant on central bank rate cuts.

text.p: Greece's money and debt markets cheered the central bank's move to cut its deposit facility rates by 30 basis points from Friday, pushing depos and treasury yields sharply lower and strenghening the drachma.

The central bank said on Thursday it would slash its basic and floor deposit facility rates to 11.6 and 9.6 percent respectively, citing a large drop in interbank surplus liquidity and wider spreads between drachma and other EMS currency rates.

The Bank of Greece introduced its two-tier depo facility on March 28, 1997 to conform with expected European Central Bank (ECB) intervention standards and cope with a large surplus liquidity in excess of 1.0 trillion drachmas ($3.5 billion) at the time.
A total of 300 billion drachmas from all credit institutions operating in Greece is absorbed at the basic rate and amounts in excess of 300 billion at the floor rate.

Interbank drachma deposits plunged 30 basis points in periods up to three-months, 20 basis points up to six months and 10 basis points for longer periods. Implied drachma rates from forex forwards followed suit with a larger drop in the long end of the yield curve.

Greek bonds and FRNs which have been battered lately rallied on the news with prices of the 10-year bond gaining 60 basis points to 95.10. FRN discount margins fell to 105 basis points over the 12-month T-bill from 120 in early trading.

"The (debt) market has bounced back with zest in reaction to the central bank's rate cuts," said Paul Saraferas, assistant treasurer at private Alpha Credit Bank. "It a positive development that makes me cautiously optimistic."

The yield spread of the Greek 10-year bond over Bunds narrowed to 408 basis points from 417 basis points before the announcement. The Athens/BTP gap also shrunk to 326 basis points after the news hit the market from 335 basis points.

"The 10-year Greek/Bund yield spread offers good value at current levels," said Saraferas who pointed out that Greece's assets markets were still exposed to the winds blowing in core European markets. "The international factor is the big unknown."

But Greece's improving macroeconomic fundamanentals coupled with current low bond price levels and signs of fatigue in other European bond markets indicated that the downward risk in Greek fixed income instruments was limited, he added.
"A further drop in the long end of the interbank depo curve will help sustain the bond rally," said Saraferas.
Other senior dealers also welcomed the central bank's rate cuts and noted that an improving current account balance would bolster the drachma and help Greek assets.

The current account deficit shrunk for the second consecutive month in April but failed to undo the disappointing performance of the first couple of months of 1997, the cumulative deficit rising 21.3 percent year-on-year to $2.28 billion in January-April.

"The central bank's move is good for the markets and coupled with the current account figures for April that came out today give a positive tone to Greece's asset markets and help the drachma," said Panayiotis Dimitropoulos, head of interest rate exposure at Bank of America, Athens.
Brokers expect the Athens bourse to advance on Friday on the news, after rising 1.68 percent on Thursday, though it closed before the rate news broke.

Improvements in liquidity conditions in the interbank market, possibly from the forex side, and the maintenance of the drachma fort policy would be another booster to asset prices, said Dimitropoulos.
The drachma advanced against the ecu, trading around 309.25/30 in late dealings after breaking decisively the 309.50 support on the news.

"The ecu/drachma trend is clearly downward and I think we will see large forex inflows on unwinding long ecu/drachma positions by London players if the drachma pierces the 309 support level," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.

But other dealers put the level that would likely trigger stop losses on ecu/drachma positions lower at the 308.70/80 level and said the forex inflows would be smaller than some local players expected.

Local dealers said some London-based banks were running long ecu/drachma positions formed in late May when heavy forex outflows prompted the central bank to intervene and sell 2.0 billion ecus or more to stem the rise of the ecu against the drachma. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 284.7 Greek Drachmas)
